### The University of Jordan

---

#### Course Information

**Course No:** 0406463  
**Course Title:** Contribution of Fatwa and Ijtihad in the Modern Era  
**Number of credit hours:** 3  

**Prerequisite course:** 0406461  

The course deals with the definition of fatwa and ijtihad, their types and conditions, the difference between them, the importance of Fatwa, the conditions of the Mufti, the conditions of the questioners, the factors influencing the Fatwa, such as customs, the environment and societies, taking into account the privacy of minorities, the skills of dealing with the questioner, al-Mustafṭi, his conditions and needs, identifying ijtihad and its legitimacy, applied models in the modern time, and institutions of contemporary ijtihad such as jurisprudence academies and Sharia bodies in Islamic finance institutions.

#### Seventh: Courses in the Foundations of Religion (Usul al-Din)

**Course No:** 0431112  
**Course Title:** Mastering the art of reciting the Holy Qur'an (1)  
**Number of credit hours:** 3  

**Prerequisite courses:** 0401098, 0401099  

This course, at its first level, provides a foundation for the concepts and basic skills needed to read and master the recitation of the Quran. It includes foundational training on topics such as seeking refuge and saying "Bismillah," rules for noon saakinah, tanween, and meem saakinah, as well as the sixteen types of elongations. Additionally, it covers general rules for proper pronunciation, with practical training on reciting Juz' 21-30 of the Quran (from Surah Al-Ankabut to the end of the Quran). Students are also required to memorize Juz' 28-29, with practical application and supervision by the instructor.

---

**Course No:** 0431213  
**Course Title:** Mastering the art of reciting the Holy Qur'an (2)  
**Number of credit hours:** 3  

**Prerequisite course:** 0431112  

At the second conceptual level, this course focuses on the articulation points and characteristics of Arabic letters and the basic skills needed for reading the Quran. It delves into the roots and depth of topics related to the characteristics of letters and their junctions, covering the concept of articulation, the mechanism of the speech apparatus in producing Arabic letters and sounds, and the precise articulation of all Arabic letters. The course also emphasizes proper tongue placement and pronunciation skills for Quranic letters. Students practice reciting the second ten parts of the Quran (Juz' 11-20, from Surah Yunus to the end of Surah Al-Qasas) and memorize Juz' 17 and 18, with practical application under the supervision and guidance of the instructor.
